subject: MedCore: follow-up on retention / deletion SLAs and SOC 2 questionnaire
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@medcorehealth.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call — data retention & compliance follow-ups

Hi Claire — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- SOC 2: you asked about our current attestations and timeline for an in-scope report. Redwood currently has a SOC 2 Type II in progress; final report expected Q4 2026. We can provide interim controls documentation and the latest bridge letter once available.
- GDPR / HIPAA: our platform supports customer-configured data residency (region pinning) and a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for covered workloads. We have procedures for minimization and account-level encryption.
- Retention & deletion: you asked how we handle short-term logs, backups, and object-level deletion. Options we discussed: 30 / 90 / 365 day retention buckets, with explicit permanent deletion windows; backups keep encrypted snapshots for 90 days by default unless otherwise specified.

Action items I think make sense:
1) Claire to share the MedCore retention baseline and any contractual deletion SLA targets (e.g., delete within X days after request/termination).
2) Redwood to initiate a formal vendor security questionnaire (we can ingest your PDF or send our security form).
3) Loop in Soojin (security) and Marcus (SE) to surface config defaults and any limitations around immutable backups or log archival.

Can you confirm the retention targets you need and whether MedCore requires deletion from backups on-request (vs. best-effort after retention window)? Happy to schedule a 30-minute follow-up if that helps.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@medcorehealth.com>

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call — data retention & compliance follow-ups

Hi Ben — thanks for the summary and for clarifying. A few specifics from our side:

- Retention: for PHI-related logs and artifacts we need a default of 90 days, with an option to extend to 1 year for audit purposes. For user-generated content (non-PHI) 30-90 days is acceptable.
- Deletion SLA: when a data-deletion request is initiated by the customer or as part of contract termination, MedCore requires confirmation of deletion from active store within 5 business days. Deletion from backups is preferred within 30 days where feasible — we understand immutable backup processes may complicate immediate purging, so we asked for documented procedures.
- SOC 2: we need the latest controls matrix + expected Type II date (Q4 2026 noted). Interim evidence (control descriptions + last testing window) would be helpful for our InfoSec review.

I've attached our vendor questionnaire (MedCore_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf). Please confirm whether Redwood prefers we submit via DocuSign/secure portal or if you can ingest the PDF and route to your security team.

Thanks —
Claire
Director, Vendor Risk & Compliance
MedCore Health

Subject: RE: MedCore vendor questionnaire + retention expectations

Hi all — thanks for the context, Ben and Claire. We've kicked off the vendor intake. Proposed plan and timeline: 

1) Acknowledge receipt (this email) and request secure upload: Claire, please use this intake link to submit the questionnaire and any additional evidence: https://redwood.sharepoint.com/sites/security/vendor-questionnaire?doc=MEDCORE-2026. We prefer the completed PDF + any SOC-related evidence (control descriptions, prior remediation notes).

2) SOC 2 evidence: Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II report is in progress (testing window closed May 2026). We can share the current controls matrix and an interim bridge letter by Jun 18. The final Type II report is expected Q4 2026.

3) Retention & deletion: short answers from Security/SE below — detailed doc attached.

- Active store deletion: we can meet a 5 business-day confirmation SLA for deletion from active object stores for the workloads MedCore will designate as PHI, given the following: MedCore must identify the objects/ids or provide a manifest. Deletion requests without manifest may require additional time for search.
- Backups: our standard snapshot lifecycle purges encrypted snapshots after 90 days. Immutable archival backups (offsite vault) have a 365-day retention by default. Due to immutability and distributed snapshot replication, on-request deletion from those archives is best-effort and may take up to 30 days depending on the archive provider and legal holds. We document exceptions in the contract.

Attachment: redwood-retention-options-v1.xlsx (shows recommended retention profiles, deletion SLA language, and suggested contract clauses).

Next steps: Ben to confirm whether MedCore will accept: 1) 5 business days for active-store deletion (with manifest requirement), and 2) 30-day best-effort for backup purges with contractual exception language for immutable archives. If not, we'll escalate to Legal for tailored language.

--
Soojin Lee
Head of Security (Vendor Risk), Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

Thanks Soojin — that all sounds reasonable and helps a lot. A few confirmations from MedCore: 

- We'll provide the completed questionnaire via your intake link today.
- MedCore accepts the 5 business-day active-store deletion SLA provided we can submit a manifest (we'll coordinate with our SRE team to produce object manifests on deletion requests).
- Regarding backups: we accept the 30-day best-effort purge for archives with the caveat that we reserve the right to include a special deletion clause in the Master Services Agreement if we determine higher assurance is required after legal review.

Please send the controls matrix and bridge letter draft when available; we'll start our internal review once we have those docs. Let's tentatively schedule a 30-minute follow-up for June 19 to close open items — Ben, can you send a calendar invite?

Best —
Claire
